subject.title: fix: plugin host commands leave orphan child processes after timeout

question: Should trusted plugin command APIs default to killing descendants on timeout, despite changing the existing public runtime and SDK-helper behavior for callers that omitted this option?
rationale: This is a public plugin API behavioral default, not only an internal host-hook repair; repository policy requires maintainer-visible compatibility direction for plugin API changes.

options.title: Approve the scoped plugin default
options.body: Keep process-tree cleanup as the plugin-command default, add the helper-level explicit opt-out and compatibility coverage, then require real descendant-process proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve existing public defaults
options.body: Leave both public APIs direct-child by default and pursue a separately approved opt-in cleanup contract for callers that need it.

options.title: Pause for plugin API direction
options.body: Hold this PR until a plugin API owner decides whether process lifetime after a timeout is a supported caller choice.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped plugin default
recommendation.body: Keep process-tree cleanup as the plugin-command default, add the helper-level explicit opt-out and compatibility coverage, then require real descendant-process proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the `PluginRuntime.system` contract makes this the strongest available routing signal for the default-behavior decision.
